newsitem.title: PERU: Gunmen threaten to kill Peru hostages - radio.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen threaten to kill Peru hostages - radio.

text.p: Guerrillas who stormed the Japanese ambassador's residence in Peru on Tuesday threatened to kill their hostages unless authorities released their colleagues from prison, a spokesman for the gunmen told local radio.

"If they do not release our prisoners, we will all die in here," the spokesman said. He said the guerrillas were holding 250 hostages inside the residence, but that could not be confirmed and authorities earlier said they believed 40 hostages were inside the compound.
Witnesses said some hostages had left the residence in small groups, including several dozen women and old people.
According to reporters at the scene one of the women who was released was the mother of Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori, who is of Japanese descent.

The attack came during a reception to honor Monday's birthday of Japanese Emperor Akihito. The reporters said the remaining hostages included Peru's agriculture and foreign ministers and the ambassadors of Brazil, Spain and Cuba.
